story.body: You looked at the two-o'clock plot, saw that you are not on it, and wrote that in the margin. You did not stay for the afternoon.

title: Read the Shrew plot and went home

participation.context: Refused a verdict, stayed out of the hall, and promised the Jackdaw.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Took base and common as praise, asked for it in writing, and swore the night before.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Kept the cold on the river, laughed at the clerk to come, and claimed Saturday.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Kept the book as written, and did not lend it.
participation.name: John Heminges

relations.quote: At the Jackdaw, after the boxes are counted.

story.body: You stood at the parlour door with Kemp, Burbage, and Heminges while two students told the thronged hall, the ambassador, the ruined dancing, and the base and common fellows. Kemp wanted it in writing and offered himself as the sorcerer. The book, the oath, and the river stayed three stories. You refused a parlour verdict, and you did not enter the hall. Before you left, you promised Burbage the act at the Jackdaw on Saturday. He said he has not heard it.

relations.quote: At the Jackdaw, after the boxes are counted.

title: Heard the Gray's Inn men at the door and refused a verdict
